text: They came to the other side of the lake, to the region of the Gerasenes.
As soon as Jesus got out of the boat, a man with an unclean spirit came out from the tombs to meet him.
He lived among the tombs, and no one could bind him anymore, not even with a chain,
because he had often been bound with shackles and chains, but had snapped the chains and broken the shackles in pieces. No one had the strength to subdue him.
Night and day, among the tombs and in the hills, he kept crying out and cutting himself with stones.
When he saw Jesus from a distance, he ran and bowed down before him,
and crying out with a loud voice, he said, "What do you want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I beg you before God, don't torment me!"
For Jesus had already told him, "Come out of the man, you unclean spirit!"
Then Jesus asked him, "What is your name?" "My name is Legion," he answered, "because we are many."
And he begged Jesus repeatedly not to send them out of the region.
A large herd of pigs was there, feeding on the hillside.
The demons begged him, "Send us to the pigs, so we may enter them."
So he gave them permission, and the unclean spirits came out and entered the pigs. Then the herd of about two thousand rushed down the steep bank into the lake and drowned in the water.
Those who tended the pigs ran off and reported it in the town and countryside, and people went out to see what had happened.
They came to Jesus and saw the man who had been possessed by the legion of demons sitting there, clothed and in his right mind, and they were afraid.
Those who had seen it described to them what had happened to the demon-possessed man, and told about the pigs as well.
Then the people began to beg Jesus to leave their region.
As Jesus was getting into the boat, the man who had been demon-possessed begged him earnestly that he might stay with him.
Jesus did not let him, but told him, "Go home to your own people, and tell them how much the Lord has done for you and how he has had mercy on you."
So the man went away and began to proclaim in the Decapolis how much Jesus had done for him, and everyone was amazed.
When Jesus had crossed again in the boat to the other side, a large crowd gathered around him while he was still by the lake.
One of the synagogue leaders, named Jairus, came, and when he saw Jesus, he fell at his feet
and pleaded with him earnestly, "My little daughter is dying. Come and lay your hands on her so that she will get well and live."
So Jesus went with him, and a large crowd followed and pressed in around him.
Now a woman was there who had had a flow of blood for twelve years.
She had suffered a great deal under the care of many doctors and had spent everything she had, yet instead of improving she had gotten worse.
When she heard about Jesus, she came up behind him in the crowd and touched his garment,
for she said, "If I just touch his clothes, I'll be made well."
Instantly her bleeding stopped, and she sensed in her body that she was healed of her affliction.
At once Jesus realized that power had gone out from him, and he turned around in the crowd and asked, "Who touched my clothes?"
His disciples said to him, "You see the crowd pressing against you, and yet you ask, 'Who touched me?'"
But he kept looking around to see who had done this.
The woman, knowing what had happened to her, came trembling with fear and fell down before him, and told him the whole truth.
He said to her, "Daughter, your faith has made you well. Go in peace and be healed of your affliction."
While he was still speaking, messengers came from the synagogue leader's house, saying, "Your daughter is dead. Why bother the teacher any longer?"
But overhearing what was said, Jesus told the synagogue leader, "Don't be afraid. Only believe."
He did not let anyone follow him except Peter, James, and John, James's brother.
They came to the leader's house, and Jesus saw a commotion — people weeping and wailing loudly.
He went in and said to them, "Why all this commotion and weeping? The child is not dead but asleep."
They laughed at him, but he put them all outside, took the child's father and mother and those who were with him, and went in where the child was.
Taking her by the hand, he said to her, "Talitha koum," which means, "Little girl, I say to you, get up."
Immediately the girl got up and began to walk — she was twelve years old — and they were utterly astonished.
He gave them strict orders that no one should know about this, and told them to give her something to eat.
